The Salon Tech Gazette.

The 1843-ish edition. Every story is invented. The editorial outrage is a performance.

FICTIONAL EDITION · 1843-ish

Everything that never happened, all in one place.

Cloud and machines01
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

Steam Cloud escapes up the chimney again.

Customers report data showers. The operator recommends a bucket and a local backup.

Read the full article

The fictional company Steam Cloud announced today that its infrastructure has moved into the upper atmosphere. The migration was unplanned and caused by a draught. File recovery will resume after the rain. The editors note that ordinary paper may not scale, but it rarely leaves the room through the chimney.

Cloud and machines02
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

Hardware arriving soon, says announcement from 1843.

The project plan has three phases: design, waiting and renaming waiting as research.

Read the full article

Our fictional supplier has unveiled a new order status: almost probably on its way. Meanwhile, programmers are testing on paper, which boasts excellent battery life. This is satire about modern projects, not a real statement by Charles Babbage or a historical news report.

Salon life03
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

Programmer declines meeting that could have been a letter.

A request for a clear meeting agenda shakes the salon. A working group has been formed.

Read the full article

A fictional committee met for two hours to decide whether to meet again tomorrow. The Ada of our alternative reality sent a single paragraph with the solution. The committee praised her initiative and proposed an hour-long presentation of the paragraph. Meanwhile, the butler solved the problem by stopping the tea refills.

Salon life04
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

Bug in machine demands recognition as a feature.

It has six legs, no documentation and very strong views on backwards compatibility.

Read the full article

In our fictional salon, a beetle refuses to move out until it gets its own ticket. It claims that unpredictable results encourage creativity. The editors suggest a safe relocation to the garden and a fix for the program. This story is not a historical account of the origin of the term bug.

Poetical Science05
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

Research: one biscuit improves reviewer's mood.

The study has one participant. He insists on an immediate repeat of the experiment.

Read the full article

In an entirely fictional experiment, an editor received a biscuit and stopped complaining about semicolons. The researchers draw no scientific conclusions, because the researchers do not exist either. The only reliable finding: the biscuits ran out before the code review comments did.

Poetical Science06
✳ INVENTED FOR THIS WEBSITE

TeaGPT promises a revolution. So far, it predicts the next sip.

The fictional model was trained on three tea leaves and one piece of society gossip.

Read the full article

The fictional service TeaGPT answers every question with it depends on the water temperature. Investors in our imaginary salon are delighted, because the answer works even when asked about the business model. The editors recommend checking claims and drinking ordinary tea without a subscription.
